title: Cuba on the Brink: Is the Regime Nearing Its Endgame? — Eddie Would Go

u.La crisis económica, los apagones y el é: Economic crisis, blackouts and mass exodus raise the question nobody in Havana wants to answer.
u.«En Cuba no solo se perseguían las ideas: «In Cuba it was not only ideas that were persecuted: joy was persecuted, desire, difference, life itself.»
u.Un reciente informe del Wall Street Jour: A recent Wall Street Journal report suggested that the Trump administration has identified Cuba as its next target for "regime change". It was followed by statements from President Trump himself, who declared the Castro regime to be "on its last legs", and even speculated that Senator Marco Rubio — the son of Cuban exiles — might one day preside over the island. The Secretary of State echoed these sentiments, hinting that the end of the Cuban regime is near. But how plausible is genuine transformation in Cuba?
u.Para comprender el presente, primero deb: To understand the present, one must first recognise the importance Cuba plays in American domestic politics. The dream of a post-communist Cuba is the founding myth of the influential Cuban-American diaspora concentrated in Florida. Their aspiration — the fall of the Castro dynasty and the island's return to democracy — has made them a vital and reliably Republican electoral bloc. Their support was instrumental in delivering Florida's electoral votes to Trump in both his campaigns. For any Republican administration, hard rhetoric on Cuba is domestic policy par excellence.
u.Sin embargo, la importancia de Cuba se e: Cuba's importance, however, extends far beyond the Florida Straits. For decades Havana has served as the ideological and operational hub for authoritarian consolidation in Latin America. The regimes in Venezuela and Nicaragua are not merely allies; they are protégés. Their repressive strategies, intelligence operations and managed emigration to defuse internal pressure are carbon copies of the manual written by the Castro brothers after 1959. Cuban support has been the crucial link in the survival of the Bolivarian project in Caracas and of the Ortega-Murillo dynasty in Managua.
u.Además, Cuba se sitúa en un peligroso ne: Cuba also sits at a dangerous geopolitical nexus. It maintains close security and economic relations with Russia, China and Iran — a troika of American adversaries — facilitating the exchange of intelligence, investment and credit just 90 miles from the American coast. This transforms Cuba from a regional nuisance into a potential base for hostile powers, a fact not lost on Washington's security establishment.
u.Un Ciclo Trágico de Intervención y Reacc: A Tragic Cycle of Intervention and Reaction
u.La relación histórica entre Estados Unid: The historical relationship between the United States and Cuba is a tragic cycle of intervention and reaction. America's war with Spain began over events in Cuba and concluded not in sovereign independence but in decades of quasi-colonial tutelage, culminating in the brutal and corrupt dictatorship of Fulgencio Batista. His overthrow by Fidel Castro in 1959 was, in part, a nationalist revolt against this history. The catastrophic Bay of Pigs invasion in 1961 severed the remaining ties and pushed Havana firmly into Moscow's arms, setting the stage for the missile crisis.
u.La supervivencia de Cuba desde entonces: Cuba's survival since then has been a story of external patronage. Soviet subsidies ended with the Cold War, plunging the island into the "Special Period" of the 1990s — an economic contraction so severe that it cut GDP by a third, according to World Bank data and studies by the Centre for the Study of the Cuban Economy. Social discontent, such as the 1994 "Maleconazo" protests, was met with a dual strategy of repression and an escape valve: the exodus of 30,000 rafters towards Florida, an event documented by the U.S. Coast Guard and the Institute for Cuban Studies at the University of Miami. This pragmatic, if cynical, manoeuvre relieved the pressure and created a political crisis for President Bill Clinton.
u.La salvación del régimen llegó con el as: The regime's salvation came with the rise of Hugo Chávez in Venezuela and the arrival of cheap Venezuelan oil in exchange for Cuban doctors and, as later emerged, intelligence and security personnel — an exchange detailed in reports by the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS). This lifeline, continued under Nicolás Maduro, allowed the Cuban state to limp on even as its own economy atrophied.
u.Con el bloqueo americano a Venezuela y l: With the American blockade of Venezuela and Maduro's disappearance, the economic crisis Havana was already experiencing can only worsen.
u.Hoy Cuba está experimentando un colapso: Cuba today is experiencing a collapse of historic proportions. Rolling blackouts last up to 20 hours a day, paralysing the water supply, according to monitoring reports from Cuba's National Office of Statistics and Information (ONEI). The sugar industry, which in 1989 produced eight million tonnes a year, is a skeletal remnant with a harvest of barely 160,000 tonnes in 2023 (2.7% of its historic capacity), as reported by ONEI and the Association of Cuban Sugar Technicians. Cement production fell by 50% between 2022 and 2023 alone, according to the same source. Tourism, a critical source of hard currency, is 72% below 2019 levels, according to figures from the Ministry of Tourism (MINTUR).
u.Esta espiral de muerte económica ha deto: This economic death spiral has triggered a demographic catastrophe that redefines the island's human capital. The "effective" population has contracted from 11.3 million to 9.9 million inhabitants between 2019 and 2024 — a 10% loss driven by mass migration of working-age citizens, according to projections and analysis by the Centre for Population and Development Studies (CEPDE).
u.En este contexto de decadencia económica: In this context of economic decay, the state's real engine is located in the Revolutionary Armed Forces (FAR), which control not only the weapons and the repressive apparatus but also the country's principal economic sectors. Through their vast business conglomerate GAESA (Grupo de Administración Empresarial S.A.), the military dominate tourism, logistics, import-export and retail.
u.Un estudio de 2024 del Instituto de Estu: A 2024 study by the Institute of Latin American Studies at Columbia University concluded that GAESA controls or is majority partner in businesses generating approximately 50% of all sales, employing 31% of the formal workforce and contributing 23% of the island's fiscal revenue. For the generals, losing political power would mean losing this vast economic empire — an unthinkable prospect.
u.El poder real se ha consolidado en una \: Real power has consolidated into a military "juntocracy" led by the GAESA conglomerate, which controls dollar flows and the strategic sectors.
u.El núcleo familiar: la sombra de los Cas: The family core: the Castro shadow in 2025
u.Mientras la presidencia de Miguel Díaz-C: While Miguel Díaz-Canel's presidency acts as a façade of renewal, real power still orbits the Castro family in a configuration blending lineage, security and business.
u.<span class=\"family-member-label\">Raúl: Raúl Castro: At 92, he remains the patriarch and "spirit of the revolution". Although he relinquished the presidency of the Communist Party in 2021, he continues to chair the National Defence Council, the supreme body for security and internal order, under article 109 of the Cuban Constitution. This position gives him a veto over all strategic decisions, especially those concerning the FAR and the security apparatus.
u.<span class=\"family-member-label\">Alej: Alejandro Castro Espín: He is the key piece in the shadows. An engineer and former military intelligence officer, he was the architect of the secret negotiations with the Obama administration that led to the thaw of 2014-2016, a role confirmed by American diplomats cited in "Back Channel to Cuba" by William M. LeoGrande and Peter Kornbluh. After briefly lowering his profile during the "Havana syndrome" episode, he has re-emerged as his father's security adviser and liaison with foreign allies such as Russia, according to intelligence analysis reviewed by the International Institute for Strategic Studies (IISS). He controls networks of influence within the Interior Ministry (MININT) and the intelligence services.
u.<span class=\"family-member-label\">Raúl: Raúl Guillermo Rodríguez Castro ("El Cangrejo"): He is the patriarch's physical and symbolic custodian. As head of his personal bodyguard and a constant presence at official events — including the reception of the bodies of military personnel killed in Venezuela — his role goes beyond security: he is the herald of dynastic continuity and a privileged channel of communication within the security apparatus, as documented in reports by the Spanish news agency EFE and the newspaper "El País".
u.<span class=\"family-member-label\">Mari: Mariela Castro: Raúl's daughter, she runs the National Centre for Sex Education (CENESEX). Her role is fundamentally one of public relations: she provides the regime with a "progressive", human-rights face for international consumption, diverting attention from political repression, a strategy analysed by organisations such as Human Rights Watch.
u.La familia extendida, a través de antigu: The extended family, through former brothers-in-law such as Luis Alberto Rodríguez López-Calleja (who died in 2022) and who ran GAESA for decades, ensured that the economic heart of the regime also remained in trusted hands. His legacy consolidates Castro control over the economy.
u.Por lo tanto, la perspectiva de un colap: The prospect of a sudden, voluntary collapse is therefore slim. The military and the family have too much to lose. There is no unified opposition figure of the stature of Venezuela's María Corina Machado; dissent is exiled, imprisoned or silenced, according to the annual reports of Amnesty International and the Inter-American Commission on Human Rights (IACHR). A spontaneous popular uprising would probably be met with brutal force, and with poor prospects of a democratic transition.
u.Para la administración Trump, la fantasí: For the Trump administration, the fantasy of a quick victory is just that: a fantasy. An American military intervention ("boots on the ground") would be politically toxic and militarily complicated against an entrenched, battle-hardened security apparatus. A more plausible strategy would be to seek a negotiated transition with a younger generation of the nomenklatura — a new Delcy Rodríguez, perhaps a Castro scion, as was tentatively explored with Alejandro during the Obama thaw. But this would be anathema to the hardline exile lobby, which demands nothing less than the total eradication of the dynasty, and hard even for the Secretary of State himself to tolerate.
u.La cruda realidad es que Cuba probableme: The stark reality is that Cuba is probably entering a prolonged, degenerative crisis. The regime will cling to power by any means necessary, presiding over the steady ruin of the nation. The world will be left to witness a slow-motion collapse, in which the end of the Castros may come not with a bang but with the last dying ember of a revolution that consumed its own children and left its people in the dark. Washington's rhetoric may accelerate the misery, but it is unlikely to write the ending. The great writer Reinaldo Arenas, from exile and from death, had already written it: Every Cuban carries within him a survivor who is at the same time a dying man.
